text:
Noah Juulsen is on his fifth NHL team, a first round pick of Montreal in 2015 whose career has mostly been about holding on. Sports Illustrated framed it well: "Noah Juulsen's Long Road Has Led to an Opportunity He Can't Afford to Waste."

In Colorado that opportunity has grown. After two games under 10 minutes in October, he has played 15 minutes or more in four of his last eight games, and the Avalanche have won five of his last ten. He brings the physical side, 41 hits and 23 blocks in 16 games, plus a hard shot (94.2 mph at his best) he rarely uses.

At five on five, Colorado has held 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, a few points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey's read from last season fits: he drew top competition (95th percentile) and his team created little offense with him out there, bottom 3% of defensemen.

He has 2 assists and no goals, which is about what you'd expect. His job is to stay steady in tough minutes on a good team, and so far the minutes keep coming.
